sections.html:
Where Interstate 15 meets US-6 in Utah County, about 50 miles south of Salt Lake City and 10 miles south of Provo, Spanish Fork has the Wasatch Range on its east side and Utah Lake to the northwest. It covers about 16 square miles at roughly 4,666 feet. Springville is about 4 miles northeast, Salem about 4.5 miles south and Payson about 6 miles southwest.

The 2020 Census counted 42,602 residents, up from 34,691 in 2010. Roughly 80.4% of homes are owner-occupied, and median value is $481,500 for 2020 to 2024, with a median gross rent of $1,489. That value is a survey median, so your house may sit well above or below it.

New building adds competition. Permits in 2022 covered 810 new homes, 190 of them single-family and 620 multi-family, so anyone selling an older house is shopping against fresh supply.

Utah County bills every address in the city, so your assessor, treasurer and recorder are the county offices in Provo. Nebo School District runs the public schools.

I-15 runs north to Salt Lake City and south toward Las Vegas, and US-6 heads east toward Denver through Spanish Fork Canyon. SR-51 and Main Street are the other gateways, and a Union Pacific rail line crosses the area. Mean commute time is 20.0 minutes by Census estimate.

Nebo School District has 15 schools inside the city: 9 elementary schools, 1 middle school, 1 junior high and 4 high schools. Spanish Fork High and Maple Mountain High are the main high schools, Spanish Fork Junior High and Diamond Fork Middle serve the middle grades, Landmark High is an alternative school, and American Leadership Academy is a K to 12 charter.

With 66 inches of snow in an average year, buyers look hard at the roof and the furnace. Have install dates ready for both.

Spanish Fork runs two separate water systems: drinking water for indoor use, and a pressurized irrigation system for lawns and landscaping. If your lot has a yard, a buyer will ask whether the irrigation connection works and what the seasonal bill looks like. The city also operates Spanish Fork Power & Light, with an average monthly residential bill of $77.11, and Spanish Fork Community Network for fiber, phone and cable. Natural gas comes from Dominion Energy.

Spanish Fork allows one ADU per single-family dwelling, and the owner must live on the property. Registration is yearly, so a buyer will want to see the current registration for any unit you advertise.

ADU requirementRule
Lot sizeAt least 6,000 square feet
Barred zonesA-E, R-4, R-5 and R-O
Off-street parkingThree spaces for an internal ADU, four for a detached ADU
RegistrationEvery year with Community Development through CitizenServe, $60 fee
Impact fees and separate electric meterNot required

The Building Division can be reached at 801-804-4540.

sections.h2: Property taxes and who to call
sections.html:
Utah County bills the tax, and the state's deadline is November 30. The tax notice is mailed between the middle and end of October. A separate valuation notice goes out earlier in the year, with instructions to appeal to the Board of Equalization.

The appeal deadline is the later of September 15 or 45 days after the valuation notice is mailed. Primary residences receive a 45% exemption, so taxable value is 55% of market value.

Delinquent amounts from prior years are not on the current bill, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure. The Treasurer is at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1200, Provo, phone 801-851-8255, and you can pay online. The Recorder is in Suite 1300, phone 801-851-8179.

In place of bank approval, the buyer shows proof of funds, so title work sets the pace. Closing runs through a title or escrow company, and the Utah County Recorder files the deed. Taxes are prorated to the closing date.

Inherited the house or moving for a new job? A flexible closing date can be worth more than a few thousand dollars of price.

Because older delinquent amounts are not printed on the current bill, a seller who thinks the account is clean can be surprised. Call the Treasurer in Provo for a payoff figure before you accept any offer. Whatever is owed comes out of your proceeds at the closing table, and the current year is divided by days of ownership between you and the buyer.

If your valuation looks high, you can still appeal to the Board of Equalization by the September 15 or 45-day deadline while the sale is in progress.

sections.h2: Selling a house with an ADU
sections.html: An ADU can help or hurt a sale depending on its paperwork. A registered unit on a lot of at least 6,000 square feet, with the owner living on site and the required parking, is something a buyer can count on. An unregistered unit, or one on a smaller lot or in a barred zone, becomes a problem to disclose. Check the registration with Community Development before you list, and pay the $60 fee if it has lapsed.

sections.h2: A cash sale, start to finish
sections.html:
Begin by telling us about the house: address, age of the roof and furnace, whether the irrigation works, and whether an ADU is involved. We reply with a written offer. Compare it with a listing's likely net, then decide. If you say yes, a title or escrow company opens the file and checks the title, and you agree on a closing date.

Bring photo ID, the payoff statement for any mortgage, your latest tax notice, ADU registration papers if there are any, and all keys and openers. The buyer does not need a bank approval, so you do not hold the date open for underwriting.

sections.h2: What Spanish Fork sellers usually run into
sections.html:
• An ADU that was never registered or that exceeds the lot rules.
  • Irrigation or yard problems that a buyer finds on a walkthrough.
  • A roof or furnace that has aged through years of heavy snow.
  • A tight budget when the seller has already bought elsewhere.

faqs.q: Is Spanish Fork in Utah County?
faqs.a: Yes. Utah County handles your property tax, valuation and deed recording, and Nebo School District runs the public schools.

faqs.q: When are Spanish Fork property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay without a penalty under the state calendar. Utah County mails the tax notice between mid and late October.

faqs.q: How many people live in Spanish Fork?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 42,602 people, up from 34,691 in 2010.

faqs.q: Can I rent out a basement apartment in Spanish Fork?
faqs.a: Only as a registered ADU. Spanish Fork requires owner occupancy, a lot of at least 6,000 square feet and annual registration for $60. Check the city's ADU page for the current rules.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Spanish Fork?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $481,500 for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024. That is a survey median, and your house may sit well above or below it.
